bib_record.title: Production Cross Section of N16 and N17

free_txt: Materials Testing Reactor (MTR).
Materials Testing Reactor (MTR).
Fission spectrum. Since the fission neutron spectrum
shows a sharply decreasing number of neutrons with
increasing energy, it is anticipated that the neutron
spectral distribution above 8 Mev will be relatively
unaffected by the moderating properties of the
region about the thimble. The results indicate that
over this range the spectral shape is essentially
described by the Watt fission neutron spectrum. The
cross section for N16 and N17 weighted with the flux
spectrum in the thimble has been determined.
N16 and N17 are obtained in the experiment by
continuously piping fresh demineralized water through
a long, thin irradiation thimble in the high, fast
neutron flux region of the Materials Testing Reactor.
The water is then piped to a flat cylindrical plastic
source disk located outside the reactor. Gamma rays
from N16 and neutrons from N17 have been detected.
From the measurements and the known geometry, the
cross sections for the 016(n,p)N16 and the 017(n,p)N17
reactions averaged over the fission neutron spectrum
have been deduced.
A continuously flowing sample of effluent cooling
water was obtained from the bottom of an NRX fuel rod
assembly. The sample passed through a solenoid valve
and into a flat cylindrical tank fabricated from
sheet aluminum. The tank and measuring equipment were
surrounded by steel and masonite shielding blocks to
reduce the neutron background at the measuring
equipment and also to provide biological shielding from
the N16 activity in the water.
The observed dose rate is corrected for background
and the O19 contribution.
An anthracene scintillation detector has been
used to measure the gamma-ray dose rate at a given
distance along the centerline of the source coil in
air.
The error quoted does not include any
uncertainty in the decay scheme, the dose-to-flux
conversion factor and the energy response of the
detector. The major portion of the error is
associated with an assumed maximum uncertainty of 1 sec
in the transport time of the water through the system.
Decay constant used is 0.0943 sec**-1.

A "long counter" has been used to measure the
fast neutron flux along the centerline of the source
coil in air. The "long counter" measures fast
neutron flux independent of the neutron energy
between 0.5 Mev and 3.0 Mev. This detector has been
calibrated with a Ra-Be and a Po-Be neutron source
of known source strengths.
The error quoted does not include any
uncertainty in the decay scheme and the energy
response of the detector. The major portion of the
error is associated with the uncertainty of the
transport time of the water through the system.
Decay constant used is 0.167 sec**-1.
